summary: Nez Perce NF lookout 7 miles NW of Moose Creek: a 20-foot tower with an L-4 cab, built 1935 and abandoned 1939; one page says it was blown down in 1957.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1939; one page says it was blown down in 1957. No source describes what remains

events.note: Dynamite used to blow the tower down, per the Forest Lookouts page

evidence.supports: about 7 miles northwest of Moose Creek Ranger Station
evidence.quote: 7 miles northwest of Moose Creek R.S.

evidence.supports: L-4 is a standard 14 by 14 foot pre-cut frame house
evidence.quote: is a standard 14 x 14 foot frame pre-cut lookout house

evidence.supports: dynamite used to blow the tower down, 1957
evidence.quote: 1957: Dynamite used to blow down the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Spelled High Springs on firelookout.com and the FFLA list, High Spring on Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page. The record keeps High Springs.

sources.title: Lookout Styles, Nez Perce National Forest

notes_for_editor: Built 1935 and abandoned 1939 agree across sources. The 1957 dynamite demolition rests on one page (Forest Lookouts). That page also has a 1921 entry 'Replaced Big Rock 62' that is unclear, so it is left out of the story. The record had only the 1939 event; the 1935 built event is new. A Nez Perce National Forest lookout table (fs.usda.gov/media/259204) gives the same 1935 and 1939 dates but was not cited. The hike-in tag is from Idaho Fire Lookouts; the site was not checked. No new photos.
